name: OXP3 Deck
description: Power limits, GPU and CPU controls, fan and charging for the ONEXPLAYER 3 through its hardware helper, per-game XeSS launch options, and guided oxp3-tool and xess-xmx-linux setup.

steps.text: In Desktop Mode, open Konsole and install Steam's hardware service, InputPlumber and the power-button daemon:
steps.command: sudo pacman -S --needed steamos-manager inputplumber steamos-powerbuttond power-profiles-daemon

steps.text: Download oxp3-hw-0.1.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst from the hw-v0.1.0 pre-release into Downloads:
Print its SHA-256 and compare it with the SHA-256 you were given for oxp3-hw 0.1.0 (testers get it separately; the release's SHA256SUMS file lists the same value). Do not install it if they differ:
Install it:
Reboot: the helper's file grants apply at boot, and steamos-manager and Steam read their setup only when they start.

instructions.title: Allow more sustained power on the charger

steps.text: Copy the helper's example limits file:
Remove the # before sustained_ac_max_w = 40. Up to 52 is allowed; above 40 use a charger of 65 W or more:
Restart the helper. On battery it keeps 35 W until the charger is back:

instructions.title: Turn the hardware helper off or remove it

steps.text: Turn it off (the fan and charging go back to Auto, the firmware's limits apply):
steps.command: sudo touch /etc/oxp3-hw/disabled && sudo systemctl stop oxp3-hw

steps.text: Turn it on again:
steps.command: sudo rm /etc/oxp3-hw/disabled && sudo systemctl start oxp3-hw

steps.text: Remove it (stopping it first puts the fan and charging back to Auto), then reboot:
steps.command: sudo systemctl stop oxp3-hw && sudo pacman -R oxp3-hw

steps.text: Open Handheld Daemon's settings (its Quick Access entry, or hhd-ui in Desktop Mode) and turn its TDP controls and fan control off. Keep Handheld Daemon itself running if it drives the controller.
Back in OXP3 Deck, choose I've handled it on its row.

Remove PowerControl's folder:

steps.text: List the installed kernels and what boots next:
Boot another kernel once. Replace PACKAGE, for example linux-cachyos-rc:
Reboot. If it does not come up, hold the power button to switch off, then on: the kernel you have now starts again.
On the kernel you want, make it the one every power-on boots:
Write oxp3-diagnose-<time>.tar.gz with the device's state and logs. Serial numbers and addresses are replaced; look through it before posting it:

instructions.title: Install the programs XeSS fast mode needs

steps.text: The installer downloads Intel's shader compiler and XeSS SDK and checks the driver with these:
steps.command: sudo pacman -S --needed curl binutils tar zstd coreutils diffutils python unzip vulkan-tools

instructions.title: Install the programs XeSS fast mode needs (Bazzite)

steps.text: The installer downloads Intel's shader compiler and XeSS SDK and checks the driver with these. Bazzite has most of them; this adds what is missing to the next boot:
steps.command: sudo rpm-ostree install --idempotent curl binutils tar zstd coreutils diffutils python3 unzip vulkan-tools

steps.text: Reboot so the new deployment starts:
Quit any game. Download the newest release, xess-xmx-linux-<version>.zip. Its project publishes no checksum:
Unpack it into a folder of its own:
Run its installer as yourself. Replace VERSION with the release's; OXP3 Deck shows the exact line. It downloads a few hundred MB:
Log out of Game Mode and back in, or reboot, so Steam starts with the new driver.
Quit any game. Download the new release and unpack it next to the old one (never over it: the running session uses its driver):
Run the old release's uninstaller. Replace OLD with its folder; OXP3 Deck shows the exact line:
Run the new release's installer. Replace NEW with its folder:
Log out of Game Mode and back in. Remove the old folder only after that.

instructions.title: Repair, switch driver or uninstall XeSS fast mode

steps.text: Repair: run the installed release's installer again in its folder. Replace PACKAGE with it; OXP3 Deck shows the exact line:
Make another patched Mesa driver the default for every game. Replace MESA with its version, for example 26.3:
Uninstall: run its uninstaller as yourself. The folder stays:
Remove an old release folder that nothing uses any more, after you logged out and back in:
After an install, update, repair or uninstall: log out of Game Mode and back in, or reboot.

instructions.title: Get GE-Proton for XeSS fast mode

steps.text: System Protons such as proton-cachyos cannot carry the XeSS add-on. Install ProtonUp-Qt:
Open ProtonUp-Qt, add the newest GE-Proton for Steam, and restart Steam.
Run the XeSS installer again so it adds its shim and hook to the new Proton (the Repair step of the XeSS card).
In the game's Properties, Compatibility, pick that GE-Proton.
In Desktop Mode, open CachyOS Kernel Manager, sched-ext, and pick scx_lavd's mode (Auto, Gaming or Power save).
Change it before you start a game: switching while a game runs can freeze it.
In Steam, open the game's Properties, General, Launch options.
Change %command to %command% (with the closing %). Until then Steam passes everything as game arguments and no XeSS setting reaches the game.
